dedupe_keys.name: amber pan european atlas of in stream barriers barrier atlas

description: The Barrier Atlas is the inventory of barriers in European rivers built by the AMBER project. The page describes it as a compilation of 630,000 unique barrier records from existing datasets, with at least 400,000 more barrier points whose locations are being modelled, and states that Europe has over one million barriers, more than 10 percent of them abandoned or obsolete. Data were gathered from local, national, regional and global databases after a survey of 36 countries, and include barrier location, type and height; the project also defined a common standard for displaying and validating barrier data. Caveats: completeness varies by country and many locations are modelled, not surveyed, and the page does not state a licence or a download route, only an interactive map. For infrastructure studies it maps dams, weirs, culverts and fords that fragment rivers, useful for river restoration planning, fish passage and the condition of small hydraulic structures. There are no related records in the catalogue yet.
